Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Houston/Galveston TX
652 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Hot and mostly dry weather will continue for the rest of the 
  work week.

- A cold front will bring slightly increased rain chances to the
  entire region late Saturday or Sunday.
 
- Next week's outlook features seasonably hot and humid conditions
  with isolated afternoon showers and storms near the coast.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 135 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

This week's weather can largely be characterized by three words:
wash, rise, repeat. Today is no exception with highs in the mid to
upper 90s and heat index values between 105-108 in most locations.
Similar to the past couple days, a modest seabreeze circulation is
expected to develop off of the Gulf and Galveston bay that could
provide just enough low-lovel convergence to initiate isolated
showers this afternoon. A complicating factor to generating precip 
today, compared the the previous couple days, is the development 
of a localized mid-level high overtop of Southeast Texas based 
around 700 mb. Staunch subsidence aloft may end up squashing all 
shower development, but we kept the 20% PoPs in the forecast since
the potential is still there. The risk of thunderstorms is even 
lower, less than 10%. The increased subsidence is also helping 
reduce the coverage of diurnal cumulus, which will likely nudge 
afternoon highs a degree or two higher than yesterday's values.

The aforementioned mid-level high is forecast to wash out this 
evening as a stronger mid- and upper-level high to our northwest
starts to break down. We will still be under a localized area of
mid-level confluence, and therefore we have lowered PoPs tomorrow
along the seabreeze circulation to below 15%. Temperature and heat 
index values tomorrow will be similar today. It's worth noting
that we do not plan to issue a heat advisory since the heat index
at most locations will remain below our advisory threshold of 108.
Despite this, we're still forecasting heat index values between 
100-108 through Saturday. At the end of the day, the human body 
and an animal's response to heat does not vary much between 107 
and 108...therefore proper heat safety messaging and precautions 
should continue to be taken regardless of the presence of an 
advisory or not.

As alluded to above, the mid-level high that has been dominating 
the local weather pattern this week will break down as a trough 
deepens over the eastern CONUS. This will allow for a rare
summertime cold front to advance as far south as the I-10 corridor 
late Saturday or Sunday. Before the front arrives late Saturday, 
compressional warming ahead of the front should result in another 
day of temperatures in the upper 90s, with a few locations peaking
in triple digits. The overall risk of sites meeting or exceeding 
100 is lower than previously indicated, but most locations in the 
forecast area have a 20-30% of reaching triple digits on Saturday.
After FROPA, it will still be hot but dew point temperatures will
be several degrees lower. This will be most evident for areas
in/near the Brazos Valley where some upper 50s dew points will 
filter into the region on Sunday.

The front will also bring increased rain chances, but I wouldn't 
get your hopes too high since PoPs are generally only 20-30%. The 
lower PoPs with this forecast update are largely a function of 
frontal timing. Most of the current guidance indicates nocturnal 
FROPA, therefore all forcing for ascent will be brought by the 
front itself. If the front is able to speed up or slow down and 
move through with basically any diurnal heating, expect PoPs to 
increase.

Unfortunately, a majority of the energy associated with the front
will move east quickly, meaning the front will become stationary 
Sunday and wash out by early next week. Next week's pattern looks 
to be more typical for this time of the year with a steady fetch 
of southerly flow moving inland from the Gulf with seasonal 
temperatures, triple digit heat index values, and daily rain 
chances along seabreeze fronts.

Bonnette

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 651 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

High pressure continues to bring VFR conditions with S-SW wind 
throughout the period. Winds become light and variable overnight but 
strengthen throughout the day on Friday with potential for 15-20kt 
gusts in the afternoon. MVFR CIGs are possible in the early morning 
as we saw today at our northern terminals but would burn off by late 
morning. An isolated SHRA with the afternoon sea breeze could occur 
but confidence is too low to include it in the current TAFs.

BSM

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 135 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Light to moderate southwesterly winds and 2-3 foot Gulf seas are
expected today and tomorrow. Southwesterly flow will increase this
weekend to around 15-20 knots, possibly higher at times. Seas may
increase to around 4 feet, with Caution Flags likely. Scattered
showers and thunderstorms are also forecast Saturday night and 
Sunday. The outlook for early next week features light to moderate 
southwesterly winds, 2-3 foot seas, and isolated showers and
storms along the sea breeze boundary each afternoon.

Bonnette

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Lake Charles LA
637 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

...New AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dangerous heat continues through Saturday with afternoon highs in 
  the mid 90s to near 100 and heat indices of 105-110F.

- A Heat Advisory is in effect for all of southeast Texas and 
  southwest, Central and south central Louisiana this afternoon.

- A few showers may develop this afternoon along the sea breeze. 
  Better precipitation chances return Sunday with afternoon pop up
  thunderstorms expected each day next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
(This evening through next Wednesday)
Issued at 1245 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

The area remains between a ridge centered over the southern
Rockies and an east coast trof, but slightly more under the upper
ridge. With the ridge not completely in control, a few showers
will be possible through the afternoon, but mainly along the sea
breeze into the Atchafalaya Basin. With sparse cloud cover, temps
have climbed into the low 90s and will continue to move into the
mid to upper 90s this afternoon. HIs are expected to top out in
the 105 to 110 range with spotty areas hitting the heat adv
criteria of 108 and higher. 

Temperatures are forecast to be around a degree or two lower at
most locations Friday, however max HIs may still briefly hit 108
at isolated locations. At this time confidence is not high enough
to issue another heat advisory, especially since 90% of the area
may not reach criteria. 

The east coast trof will allow a weak boundary to drift into the
area late Saturday. Ahead of the boundary Saturday afternoon, 
compressional heating may push the I-10 corridor to the coast well
into heat adv criteria. Cloud cover moving in during during Sat 
afternoon over deep SE TX and Cen LA may hold max apparent temps 
just shy of criteria.

Rain chances increase Saturday evening into early Sunday as the
boundary moves in. More typical temps and precip chances are
expected for next week.

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 634 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

A couple of small showers may develop in the vicinity of LFT and
ARA over the next couple of hours, but will diminish by 02Z.
Otherwise, high pressure over the northeastern gulf and ridging
aloft will maintain VFR conditions through the taf period along 
with light south southwesterly winds.

Jones 

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1245 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

A light southwest flow will remain in place into Saturday evening,
however a weak boundary may move into the coastal waters early
Sunday with a brief period of offshore winds. South to SW winds 
will occur again by Sunday evening and last into the middle of
next week.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1245 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Hot and generally dry weather is anticipated through Saturday,
however an isolated shower will be possible along the sea breeze.
A weak boundary will move into the area Saturday night into early
Sunday morning with scattered thunderstorms possible.
